title: Modified Moore Swab Method for Microbiological Surface Waters Sampling
author: Enrique Delgado
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bpw9mph6

steps.title: Prepare filtration cloth
steps.instruction: Prepare the cheesecloth swab by folding and rolling.

substeps.instruction: Cut a 92 x 95 cm2 cheesecloth grade #90 piece and fold it horizontally.
Fold it again to half size and stretch.
Fold each side until they touch and press flat.
Tightly roll the cheesecloth into a cylindrical shape-swab approximately 12 cm long and 4.4 cm in diameter.

steps.title: Sterilize filtration cloth
steps.instruction: Sterilize the prepared cheesecloth using an autoclave.

substeps.instruction: Wrap the folded cheesecloth in Kraft paper.
Seal the paper with masking tape and attach sterilization indicator tape.
Autoclave at 121 ºC for 20 min.
Allow the cheesecloth to cool to room temperature.

steps.title: Assemble Modified Moor Swabs (MMS)
steps.instruction: Assemble the PVC MMS unit using specified parts.

substeps.instruction: Seal PVC tube joints using Oatey PVC and CPVC Purple Primer.
Place a Phifer BetterVue Insect screen on the wide end of the filtering unit and fix it with a rubber band.

steps.title: Sterilize MMS units and screens
steps.instruction: Chemically sterilize the MMS units and screens.

substeps.instruction: Immerse empty MMS and insect screens in a 10% chlorine solution for 30 min in a bucket, ensuring full submersion.
Transfer MMS to a dry bucket (previously washed and sterilized with chlorine) to air dry.

steps.title: Load and store MMS units
steps.instruction: Aseptically assemble the final sampling unit.

substeps.instruction: Using sterile tweezers and gloves, place the sterilized cheesecloth cylinder into a sterilized MMS.
Place the MMS into a sterile bag and close it until field sampling is required.

steps.title: Set up field sampling equipment
steps.instruction: Position the pump and connect the tubing.

substeps.instruction: Securely place the peristaltic pump and battery at the sampling location.
Couple the PVC vinyl tubing to the pump, placing one end of the tubing inside a bucket.
Couple a sterile MMS unit to the other end of the peristaltic pump tubing.
Tie the filtering unit to a 1-1.5-m stick using rope to prevent it from being dragged by the stream.

steps.title: Filter surface water
steps.instruction: Perform the water filtration process using the pump.

substeps.instruction: Submerge the MMS unit in water using the stick, grabbing the unit by its narrow part to avoid contamination.
Turn on the pump at maximum flow for 1-2 min to fill the unit and eliminate air bubbles.
Reduce speed to nearly half flow; use a 1-L container and chronometer to adjust flow to 0.5 L/min.
Direct water exit to a 14-L bucket and continue filtering until the water reaches the 10-L mark (approximately 20 min).
Turn off the pump, remove the MMS unit from the water, and uncouple it from the tubing.

steps.title: Collect and transport sample
steps.instruction: Secure the used MMS unit for transport.

substeps.instruction: Wearing new gloves, carefully place the MMS unit inside a sterile plastic bag identified with the sample name, avoiding the inner part of the bag.
Close the bag and place it in an insulated container with coolant gels for refrigeration during transport.
Empty the pump's tubing completely (hold vertically if necessary) and pack equipment.

steps.title: Record site data
steps.instruction: Log sampling details using the Epicollect5 App.

substeps.instruction: Sign in as a sample collector and create a new entry.
Record: full name of collector, sample name, date and time, GPS coordinates, and a picture of the location.

steps.title: Measure pH and temperature
steps.instruction: Analyze a separate water sample for pH and temperature.

substeps.instruction: Collect ≈0.5 L of water in a 1-L container from the same spot as the MMS, sampling far from where you are standing to avoid sediment.
Rinse a calibrated pH meter probe with distilled water using a wash bottle and dry with a disposable paper towel.
Turn on the pH meter, place it in the sample, and slowly shake for about 30 s.
Read and record pH and temperature in Epicollect5.

steps.title: Measure water turbidity
steps.instruction: Determine water turbidity using a turbidimeter.

substeps.instruction: Fill a cuvette to the mark with distilled water (handle by the head only); if touched, rinse with distilled water and dry with a paper towel.
Measure distilled water turbidity and set as the blank (zero turbidity).
Fill a 100-mL graduated cylinder with sampled surface water and use it to fill another cuvette.
Measure turbidity and record in Epicollect5.

steps.title: Perform turbidity dilutions
steps.instruction: Dilute samples if turbidity is out of range (too high).

substeps.instruction: For 1:10 dilution: Pour 10 mL of sampled water into a graduated cylinder and fill to 100 mL with distilled water.
For 1:100 dilution: Pour 10 mL of the 1:10 dilution into another graduated cylinder and fill to 100 mL with distilled water.
